title: Rudimentary organs are relatively larger in the embryo than in the adult

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Rudimentary organs are relatively larger in the embryo than in the adult

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: As a universal rule, a rudimentary part is relatively larger compared with adjoining parts in the embryo than in the adult, and some rudiments (such as the teeth of whales and ruminants) appear in the embryo and then wholly disappear.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It is also, I believe, a universal rule, that a rudimentary part or organ is of greater size relatively to the adjoining parts in the embryo, than in the adult

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “RUDIMENTARY ORGANS; their origin explained”. Scope: rudimentary organs in animals and plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-24: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The universal quantitative prediction is highly falsifiable. Public developmental data can test examples but lack representative coverage of animal and plant rudiments.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure each rudiment relative to homologous adjoining structures across embryonic and adult stages and record transient rudiments that disappear. Any robust case with a smaller relative embryonic rudiment refutes the universal rule.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Choice of adjoining-part denominator can change relative-size conclusions.

Ontogenetic series of known rudiments are sparse outside model organisms.

fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.32
operationalizability: 0.9
discriminating power: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.48
data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Embryo-versus-adult relative size is an unambiguous measurement, and a modest number of counterexamples would challenge a claimed universal rule. Public scans and matrices cover some skeletal rudiments and miss most soft or transient ones. The decision criterion is strong; the missing compilation of developmental series is what limits the test to a subset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For a pre-specified list of rudimentary organs, compare each organ's size relative to neighbouring parts in late embryos and in adults, including organs that are present in the embryo and absent in the adult. The claim is confirmed if relative size is larger in the embryo in nearly every case, and refuted by a substantial set of rudiments that are relatively larger in the adult or absent in the embryo.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Relative size depends on which adjoining landmark is chosen, and that choice can change the ratio.

Developmental series of rudiments are scattered through individual papers and are not a single analysis-ready table.

Organs that appear only as embryonic buds, such as tooth germs, are mostly in histological collections rather than in public 3D archives.
